title: RE Sae H. Han v. Korean Eastern Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC denied Han’s complaint and affirmed Korean Eastern Presbytery’s decisions concerning Lee’s stated-supply status, its clarification of its prior action, and its appointment of the Pulpit (Stated Supply Approval) Commission. It did not adjudicate later actions of that commission.
first_summary: RE Han challenged Korean Eastern Presbytery’s treatment of TE Lee as stated supply rather than pastor and its appointment of a Pulpit Commission. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery. Lee had not received an approved pastoral call or installation, and BCO 22 treated interim pastor as stated supply, limited to one year unless renewed. BCO 15-2 also permitted Presbytery to assign approval of stated-supply requests to a commission.
summary: RE Han challenged Korean Eastern Presbytery’s treatment of TE Lee as stated supply rather than pastor, its clarification of its earlier action, and its appointment of a Pulpit Commission. The SJC denied the complaint and affirmed Presbytery: Lee lacked an approved pastoral call or installation, “interim pastor” meant stated supply under BCO 22, and his unrenewed one-year term had expired. BCO 15-2 permitted the commission’s appointment to process stated-supply requests. The ruling did not approve or disapprove the commission’s later actions.

sources.supports: Case 2007-07’s issues, denial and affirmance, adopted reasons, and limitation concerning later commission actions.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The joint heading identifies Cases 2007-1, 2007-6, and 2007-7 and the parties; section C identifies 2007-7 as Han’s complaint (printed pp. 92, 98; lines 13, 164–168).
evidence_notes.dispute: Han alleged premature dissolution, contradictory Presbytery decisions, and improper appointment of a pulpit commission (printed p. 95; lines 82–86).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The complaint was denied and KEP affirmed; earlier reasoning classified Lee as stated supply, while BCO 15-2 supported appointing the commission (printed pp. 97–98; lines 140–168).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC ruled only on proper appointment, not pending complaints about subsequent commission actions (printed p. 95; lines 108–109).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Section C expressly adopts the supplied reasoning stated earlier in the same joint decision concerning Lee’s status and KEP’s clarification (printed p. 98; lines 164–168).

source_limits: The source is a joint opinion for three complaints. Case 2007-07 adopts reasoning developed earlier in that opinion, but the incorporated reasoning and result are supplied. Later commission actions remained outside this decision.
